campaign.062d.scenario.ruscam00.xml.intr: The campaign has reached a point where speed matters as much as firepower. The Soviet counteroffensive is gathering force. The time for retreating is over, now we must drive the fascist beasts from the soil of the Motherland! Now we began with Operation Uranus here on the Chir. The wider stakes are clear: The Soviet 21st Army and 5th Tank Army were able to capture some 27,000 Romanian prisoners�the bulk of three divisions�and then continue their advance southwards. Concentrate your best units, protect the flanks of the advance, and seize the decisive objectives before the enemy can rebuild a line.
campaign.062d.scenario.ruscam00.xml.outc:
Very good General! STAVKA will be pleased at this news, the breakthrough here has trapped hundreds of thousands of fascist troops in Stalingrad.

The Third Romanian Army began to be routed by the end of 19 November. The Soviet 21st Army and 5th Tank Army were able to capture some 27,000 Romanian prisoners the bulk of three divisions and then continue their advance southwards. Soviet cavalry was used to exploit the breakthrough, sever communications between the Romanians and the Italian 8th Army, and to block any possible counterattack against the Soviet flank.
Comrade General, STAVKA has sent these NKVD troops for you, I'm afraid you have been relieved of command...

Comrade, while this can be called a victory, it has failed to impress STAVKA and many more victories such as this will mean we will not have an army to fight with. You must do better by our people and for the Motherland!

Soviet cavalry was used to exploit the breakthrough, sever communications between the Romanians and the Italian 8th Army, and to block any possible counterattack against the Soviet flank.

Comrade General! Victory is sweet, no? However, if you had moved quicker it would have been more brilliant, but STAVKA approves. We have destroyed many fascist forces and trapped German troops in Stalingrad.

campaign.062d.scenario.ruscam01.xml.intr: The initiative is yours, but the enemy will not remain disorganized for long. The Soviet counteroffensive is gathering force. Now is the time to crush the Italians. General Fyodor Isidorovich Kuznetsov's 1st Guards Army and General Dmitri Danilovich Lelyushenko's 3rd Guards Army attacked from the north, encircling 130,000 soldiers of the Italian 8th Army on the Don and advancing to Millerovo. (Manstein sent the 6th Panzer Division to the Italians' aid of the 130,000 encircled troops, 45,000 survived to join the Panzers at Chertkovo on 17 January). Momentum is your greatest asset: pause too long and a breakthrough becomes another costly frontal battle.
